title: SLO Atlas: per-endpoint SLI enrichment, burn-rate forecasting, and cross-region preemption policy
creator: Marco Reyes
description:
Background: We lack a standardized, machine-readable SLO/SLI surface that ties per-endpoint request types (chat, streaming, embeddings) to burn-rate forecasts and an automated cross-region preemption policy. This ticket defines the SLI enrichment model, error-budget math, circuit-breaker thresholds, and a preemptive regional shedding algorithm to be implemented alongside the runtime admission controller.

Goals:
1) Define canonical SLIs per endpoint: availability (5xx + routing failures) at p99/p95 latency buckets, tail latency (p99.9) for streaming attach points, and correctness proxies (regression rate vs golden promptset) as an optional quality SLI.
2) Provide a deterministic error-budget calculator that consumes current burn rate, backlog, and regional capacity to output a reclaimable token budget and recommended preemption windows.
3) Specify circuit-breaker trigger tiers and preemption order: local soft-shedding -> regional preempt -> cross-region reroute -> degrade-to-quantized-variant.
4) Produce an orchestration policy for cross-region preemption that respects tenant isolation, reserved dedicated capacity, and customer tiers.

SLI definitions (proposed):
- Availability SLI (per-route): success_rate = 1 - (5xx_count + routing_errors) / total_requests. Target 99.9% monthly for tier-1 low-latency routes.
- Latency SLI: p95 and p99 over request service_time (end-to-end), with tail SLI p99.9 tracked for conversational attach points.
- Quality SLI (optional): promptset_regression_rate computed via scheduled evals; target <= 1% regression over baseline.

Error budget math:
- Monthly budget = 1 - SLO_target. Burn rate computation uses time-weighted error budget consumption with half-life smoothing over 1h windows and 24h lookback for forecasts. Forecast output: time_to_breach (minutes) and probability_of_breach (0-1).

Circuit breakers and thresholds (proposed):
- Advisory tier: burn_rate >= 0.5 triggers advisory alert to oncall.
- Soft-shedding tier: burn_rate >= 1.0 -> enable per-route queue caps and increase reject_fraction by small increments up to 10%.
- Regional preempt tier: burn_rate >= 2.0 or time_to_breach <= 30m -> trigger cross-region preemption logic (if capacity available).
- Hard-fail tier: sustained burn_rate >= 5.0 for 15m -> open circuit for non-critical low-tier routes, divert traffic to degraded variants.

Cross-region preemption policy:
- Preemption respects pinned dedicated pools and customer SLA tiers. Preemption ordering: best-effort public -> experimental variants -> low-tier customers -> traffic steering to other regions with compatible model variants.
- Preemption step-down window: 60s to 3m per step (configurable).

Observability and alerts:
- Dashboards: per-endpoint SLI time-series (p95/p99/p99.9), burn-rate gauge, forecasted time_to_breach heatmap, and preemption decisions log.
- Alerts: PagerDuty for time_to_breach <= 30m on tier-1 routes; Slack escalation channel for advisory tiers.

Runbooks and testing:
- Attach runbook links: (draft) Confluence: /reliability/slo-atlas-runbook; will link after PR.
- Testing plan: unit tests for error-budget math, integration tests simulating regional capacity loss, and a chaos run (staging) to validate preemption order.

Open questions / decisions needed: 
- Should quality SLI be enforced as part of the same error budget or tracked separately with a quality escrow? (PM input required)
- Exact weighting for p99.9 tail in composite SLI (ops vs product trade-off).
- Acceptable maximum reject_fraction for low-latency routes during soft-shedding.

Deliverables:
- SLO Atlas JSON schema (machine-readable SLI declarations) and a reference implementation in the admission controller.
- Runtime flags for circuit-breaker thresholds and preemption sequencing.
- Updated dashboards and pager rules.

Stakeholders: SRE (primary), Runtime infra, Product (latency SLAs), Support (customer comms).
